newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel details Philippine bank deal. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Keppel details Philippine bank deal. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]

text.p: Keppel Corp said on Friday its wholly-owned subsidiary, Kephinance (Corrects name from Keppel Finance Ltd) would take a 30-percent stake in its purchase of Philippines Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank.

Wang Look Fung, Keppel's general manager of public affairs, told Reuters the group's Philippines unit, Keppel Philippines, was also likely to take a 30-percent stake and the remaining would be held by Keppel IVI, its investment merchant bank.
On Thursday, the group signed a rescue package for Philippines second oldest bank.
The Keppel Corp agreed to inject one billion pesos to eliminate the bank's negative networth while the Philippines central bank will inject 1.5 billion pesos, Wang said.
Keppel will own 60 percent of the bank and will have as its local partner Vicent Tan, who owned a majority in the bank.
The deal is expected to increase Keppel's banking presence in the Philippines. Keppel has 31 branches there.
